title: Smith obtained subpoenas to access communication records of mostly Republican lawmakers
text:
The Department of Justice (DOJ) received a submission of a criminal referral regarding James G. Smith, a former DOJ employee. The referral was made by Senator Sheldon S. whitehouse and Senator Sheldon S. Whitehouse. The DOJ has confirmed the allegations stating that Smith lied to Congress about his actions regarding personal messages of lawmakers. the text messages that Smith claims to not have accessed were related to White Home personell phone records. The DOJ is investigating Smith due to alleged perjury and misconduct. The submitted criminal referral is due to new evidence related to Smith's period at the President Bidens DOJ. The investigation started after allegations of potential election interference in the 2020 US Presidential Election in the Jan. 6 case. James G. Smith is being investigated by the DOJ for reviewing personal text messages of 44 lawmakers. The Senate Judiciary Committee and House Judiciary Committee issued subpoenas regarding his actions. The Senate is currently investigating the potential abuse of the justice system to investigate Senator Ron Dean's statements in the Jan. 6 investigation. The DOJ reAds his colleagues' text messages. The US Congress is investigating potential illegal actions during the 2020 US Presidential Election. the DOJ is preparing to subpoena House Speaker Kevin McCarthy's cellphone for his discussions around Capitol Hill
to the Department of Justice over allegations he lied to Congress about tracking personal phone messages of dozens of lawmakers. Republicans have long raised concerns about Smith’s time at President Joe Biden’s DOJ.
Smith obtained subpoenas that allowed him to access communications records of mostly Republican lawmakers as part of the DOJ’s and FBI’s “Arctic Frost” investigation. Before saying last week that records prove Smith’s team reviewed personal text messages of 44 lawmakers, Grassley had said Smith issued 197 subpoenas to 34 individuals and 163 businesses, including financial institutions, as part of Arctic Frost, in conjunction with former FBI Director Christopher Wray. The subpoenas requested records and communications related to over 430 individuals and organizations, ”all of them appear to be aimed at Republicans,” according to Grassley.
Cruz said last November that, in the investigation, U.S. District Judge James Boasberg signed off on subpoenas from Smith’s office that held “no basis,” ordering phone companies to allow the government to monitor the phone lines of“When you have the Biden Department of Justice subpoenaing 20% of the Republicans in the Senate, it is an egregious abuse of process,” Cruz said.
